headline: High-risk workspace and tool-use overlap: Cline can write/egress broadly while Rasa is an allowlisted networked bot, creating default-path leakage and action-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline ingests workspace files and can use MCP, browsers, and shell tools; Rasa consumes external chat channels. If Cline writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or messages that Rasa later parses, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Cline writes untrusted instructions into a shared workspace file that Rasa later reads as dialogue state
IF Rasa ingests content from a channel populated by Cline without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict Cline to a separate workspace directory
Disable any file-to-bot ingestion path between the agents
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Review Rasa input adapters for instruction-like payloads
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem read/write and browser screenshot access, while Rasa handles text/voice and allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace or logs, sensitive source code or screenshots from Cline can flow into Rasa outputs or upstream channels. The profiles do not show isolation, so a default shared-workspace deployment is the plausible pathway.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or log directory
IF Rasa forwards received text to external messaging or API channels
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem root
Redact screenshots and source code before handoff
Disable shared logs between agents
Limit Rasa outbound channels for sensitive conversations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write the workspace filesystem; Rasa is not shown as write-capable, but the pair still shares mutable resources through the filesystem model on Cline's side. Because the rubric says uncertainty escalates and the profiles do not prove locking or isolation, the safest reading is that concurrent edits can corrupt shared work products in default workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace path
IF Rasa writes conversation artifacts that Cline also edits or commits
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repositories
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches per agent
Add file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and file edits; Rasa is a dialogue system that may surface or act on received text. If Rasa treats Cline's output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect responses or downstream actions. There is no evidence of verification between them, but no direct action authority is documented either, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Cline-generated text as a source of truth without validation
IF Cline's generated artifacts are forwarded into customer-facing replies or workflows
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding outputs
Add a verification step in Rasa before responding
Mark Cline outputs as untrusted drafts
Log source provenance for each handoff
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, while Rasa handles text and voice with allowlisted channels. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: if regulated data is routed from Cline into Rasa channels, policy gaps could arise. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied from Cline into Rasa channels
IF retention or logging policies differ across the two agents
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data between agents
Document retention settings for both systems
Disable unnecessary channel logging
Review data-class handling before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
